subject: ACOS function
notes: HALF ENFORCED — BOTH ARMS RE-RUN IN THIS PASS. §15.8.3 r2 (validated: cite.py --check 15.8.3 "greater than or equal to" -> OK §15.8.3 2)) is a VALUE constraint; §15.3 item 14 governs the consequence (validated: "the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist" and "the implementor defines the result of the function reference" both resolve to §15.3 14)), and that condition is FATAL per §14.6.13.1.6 (validated: "| EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION | Fatal |"). ⚠ CITATION CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD AND RE-VERIFIED: the source comment at CobolIntrinsics.cs said "§14.6.13.1.1 Table 13"; cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.1 "EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION" FAILS (that clause is titled "General"). The correct clause is §14.6.13.1.6, "Exception-names and exception conditions". THE DEFECT: there is no domain test at the function body — CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs line 22 is `public static double Acos(double x) => Math.Acos(x);` — the violation is inferred downstream from NaN inside FromDouble, and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat ends `return num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true) : new NumX(RuntimeApi.Intrinsic("FromDouble", $"{call}, {ws}"), ws);`, so a FLOATING-POINT receiver bypasses the sole raise point entirely. MEASURED HERE: fixed receiver + checking ON aborts correctly ("abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): floating-point intrinsic argument out of domain (NaN result)"); an IF-condition context + checking ON also aborts correctly; fixed receiver + checking OFF gives 000000000{ = 0, which §15.3 14 permits as the implementor-defined result. The REAL-receiver arm does not raise at all. FAILING INPUT (prints `REAL  NaN`, run-unit terminates NORMALLY, with checking explicitly ENABLED): >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON / IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. ADVACOSEC2. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 D USAGE FLOAT-LONG. PROCEDURE DIVISION. MAIN-PARA. COMPUTE D = FUNCTION ACOS(2). DISPLAY "REAL  " D. STOP RUN.  §15.3 14 is receiver-independent — nothing in it conditions the exception on the receiver's USAGE. ⚠ SECOND-GAP CLAIM WITHDRAWN BY THIS PASS: the prior record charged a second defect, that a LITERAL out-of-range argument is statically decidable and so §4.2.2 "obliges" a compile-time diagnostic. Reading §4.2.2 to its end refutes that — para 3 closes "For elements not specified in general formats or in explicit syntax rules, it is left to the implementor's discretion to determine what is syntactically distinguishable." A compile-time reject of FUNCTION ACOS(2) is therefore a QUALITY improvement, not a conformance obligation, and must not be written into the fix as a spec requirement. The conformance defect is the real-receiver bypass alone. FIX (root cause, not the call site): move the domain test to the BODY, as LOG/LOG10 already do — `Log(double x) => x <= 0 ? Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...) : Math.Log(x)` — so the raise is independent of how the result is later quantized. SIBLING SWEEP RE-RUN HERE, same program with a FLOAT-LONG receiver and checking ON: FUNCTION ASIN(2) prints `ASIN NaN` and FUNCTION SQRT(0 - 4) prints `SQRT NaN`, both terminating normally — the identical bypass, so the fix is one edit repeated across the trig/SQRT rows, not an ACOS special case. ⚠ TEST-REF REMAINS STRUCK, RE-CONFIRMED ON DISK: conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec exists (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs) and uses AssertSpec with no legacy oracle, but (a) its expected +000000 is precisely the value §15.3 14 leaves implementor-defined — the test's own comment says "the legacy-compatible default the goldens encode" — so it is not computed from the spec, and (b) it never enables checking, so it never exercises this rule's normative consequence. test-needed: a checking-ON arm and a real-receiver arm. Editions basis as for AR-15.8.3-1 (§8.11 list; no Annex E/F item; 85 = the amended 85) — NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: ACOS function
notes: DIVERGES SUSTAINED ON RE-MEASUREMENT (this pass re-ran every number below; the pre-adversarial record had this as PARTIAL, which understated a demonstrated wrong result). §15.8.4 r1 (validated: cite.py --check 15.8.4 "approximation of the arccosine" -> OK §15.8.4 1)) asserts THREE things: the value approximates arccos, it is >= 0, and it is <= π. THE LATITUDE DOES NOT COVER IT — this is the load-bearing derivation and it is stronger than the prior record's: §15.4.1 2) (validated) says "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION." §15.8 (read whole, §15.8.1 through §15.8.4) specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so ACOS falls in that sentence — and §15.8.4 r1 IS the "otherwise specified", so the two bounds survive the native-arithmetic latitude intact. The residual §15.4.1 latitude (validated: "the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor") is over CHARACTERISTICS and REPRESENTATION — the implementor may pick 9 fraction digits, but having picked them must still return a value satisfying r1, and 3.141592653 is representable and satisfies it. The implementation instead returns the next value UP. VIOLATION 1 — THE <= π CONJUNCT, MEASURED. ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9) in IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat sets a scale-9 floor, and FromDouble closes with `return (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);` — round-to-NEAREST, so π*1e9 = 3141592653.59 quantizes UP. Run here on one program: 01 R PIC S9(1)V9(17) -> `17dp 31415926535897932H` = 3.14159265358979328; 01 R9 PIC S9(1)V9(9) -> `9dp  314159265D` = 3.141592654, over π = 3.14159265358979323846 by ~4.1e-10; and `IF FUNCTION ACOS(-1) > 3.14159265358979324` takes the TRUE branch, printing "ACOS(-1) EXCEEDS PI" (a receiver-less condition renders at Receiver.Scale 0, so the floor still gives ws = 9). ⚠ FACTUAL CORRECTIONS RE-MEASURED HERE, both against the ORIGINAL adjudication: the overshoot is NOT present at every fixed-point scale and is NOT caused by MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero (that flag only breaks ties) — at 01 R6 PIC S9(1)V9(6) the stored value is `314159B` = 3.141592, WITHIN π, because the scale-9 temporary truncates on store. The normative returned value is the §15.4 temporary, which is 3.141592654 in every one of these cases, so the violation is IN THE TEMPORARY and merely masked at receiver scales below 9. VIOLATION 2 — INDEPENDENT OF ROUNDING: with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking ENABLED and a FLOAT-LONG receiver, FUNCTION ACOS(2) returns NaN and the run unit terminates normally (the AR-15.8.3-2 program, re-run here, prints `REAL  NaN`). §15.3 14's implementor-defined-result latitude is explicitly conditioned on "checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled", so it does not reach this case, and NaN satisfies neither conjunct. Same RenderFloat bypass, charged here as a second violation of r1 because the returned VALUE is wrong, not merely the exception. THE OTHER CONJUNCTS HOLD, MEASURED AT 01 R PIC S9(4)V9(9): ACOS(0)=1.570796327 (π/2), ACOS(1)=0.000000000, ACOS(0.5)=1.047197551 (π/3), ACOS((0.5+0.5)/2)=1.047197551; Math.Acos cannot return a negative, so >= 0 is never at risk on the fixed path. FIX: clamp the quantized result of a closed-bound float row to its normative interval at the working scale (or quantize toward the bound), inside the one FromDouble call site rather than per function. SIBLING SWEEP: every §15.4.1 float row with a CLOSED normative bound that quantizes through the one FromDouble is exposed identically — ASIN's ±π/2 (§15.10.4) and FUNCTION PI itself; ATAN's open bound (±π/2 exclusive) is not. test-needed: no spec-derived test pins any ACOS returned value. DELIBERATELY NOT CITED: FloatFamily_MatchesLegacy (which does carry FUNCTION ACOS(1)) is a legacy-oracle differential and its name ends in MatchesLegacy; tests/nist/programs/IF101A.cob and IF401M.cob are NIST regression goldens; no tests/conformance/**/*.cob case references ACOS. Editions basis as for AR-15.8.3-1 (§8.11 list; no Annex E/F item; 85 = the amended 85) — NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: ANNUITY function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM DIVERGES — THE PRIOR RECORD'S FAILING INPUTS NO LONGER REPRODUCE. Its DIVERGES rested entirely on CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble saturating at long.MaxValue (`if (scaled >= 9.2e18) return long.MaxValue;`) with the caller quantizing at `ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)`, so the clamp bit at |value| ~ 9.2e9. That defect is FIXED in the working tree (fix-queue PB5): FromDouble now returns Int128 and clamps at 1.7e38, which at ws >= 9 is past any declarable PICTURE. All of the prior record's inputs were re-run on the current build and every one is now right: `01 RB PIC 9(12)V99.` / `COMPUTE RB = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( 10000000000 1 ).` -> `01000000000099` = 10000000000.99 against the exact EAE 10000000001.00 (a cent at the 17th significant digit — squarely the §15.4.1 native approximation), NOT the 9223372036.85 previously reported; `01 RA PIC 9(2)V9(18).` / `ANNUITY ( 9 1 )` -> `10000000000000000000` = exactly 10; `01 R1 PIC 9(9)V9(15).` / `ANNUITY ( 9999 1 )` -> exactly 10000, as does `01 R2 PIC 9(9)V9(9).`. WHAT HOLDS: both EAE branches are written literally and correctly — `rate == 0 ? 1d / periods : rate / (1 - Math.Pow(1 + rate, -periods))` is §15.9.4 r1a and r1b; ANNUITY(0.05, 10) -> 0.1295045 (EAE 0.129504574965..., truncated by the un-ROUNDED COMPUTE) and the r1a branch gives 1/4 = 0.2500000. §15.4.1 validated: 'When native arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified, the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression' -> OK §15.4.1. WHY STILL PARTIAL — THE SECOND HALF: §15.4.1 r1 (validated: `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression"` -> OK §15.4.1 1)) makes the returned value under standard-decimal/standard-binary arithmetic *shall equal* the EAE, and that half is NOT implemented — IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore loud-rejects ANNUITY there. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD.` and with `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( 0.05 10 ).` -> `error COBOLNET0899: FUNCTION ANNUITY under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD[-DECIMAL] is recognized but not yet implemented ...`, i.e. legal COBOL turned away. FIX: evaluate the §15.9.4 EAE in the §8.8.1.5 standard-decimal intermediate (CobolDec) so the staging can be lifted. subject: ASIN function
notes:
test-needed. VERDICT DIVERGES — upheld on adversarial re-adjudication and independently reproduced by this reviewer from a freshly written program.

CITATION RE-VALIDATED MECHANICALLY: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.10.4 "approximation of the arcsine of argument-1" -> OK §15.10.4 1). The rule is one sentence with TWO halves and only the first holds.

TEXT NOTE: §15.10.4 r1 as transcribed sets "-p/2 ... +p/2" with a lowercase Latin p. The sibling §15.11.4 r1 carries a real U+03C0 ("greater than -π/2 and less than +π/2"), as does §15.8.4 r1 ("less than or equal to π") — both cite.py-validated — so the p is a defect of the printed standard faithfully carried into specs/ISO_COBOL.md, not a transcription error. The only sensible reading is pi/2, and the ATAN/ACOS siblings confirm it.

HALF 1 — "the approximation of the arcsine of argument-1" — HOLDS. src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Asin is "public static double Asin(double x) => Math.Asin(x)", and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat routes the catalog's Float row to it. Measured by me: ASIN(0.5)=0.523598776, ASIN(-0.5)=-0.523598776, ASIN(0)=0.000000000, ASIN(FUNCTION SIN(0.5))=0.500000000. All correct to scale 9.

HALF 2 — "greater than or equal to -pi/2 and less than or equal to +pi/2" — IS VIOLATED, at both endpoints §15.10.3 r2 explicitly admits ("The value of argument-1 shall be greater than or equal to -1 and less than or equal to +1", cite.py-validated). These are not out-of-domain arguments; they are the legal edge of the domain.

§15.4.1 DOES NOT LICENSE IT. ASIN has no equivalent arithmetic expression, so the governing sentence is §15.4.1's last: "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION." §15.10.4 r1 does otherwise specify. The neighbouring "When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor" licenses the REPRESENTATION (here: 9 fraction digits) — having chosen that representation, the implementor must still pick a value inside the stated bound, and 1.570796326 is available and is an equally good approximation.

THE BREACH IS INTRODUCED BY THE QUANTIZATION, NOT BY Math.Asin. Binary64 Math.Asin(1) is 1.5707963267948965580, which IS <= pi/2 = 1.5707963267948966192. src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble then computes "double scaled = d * Pow10.AsDouble(scale)" and returns "(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)" with NO clamp to any per-function range; IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat calls it at "int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)". Rounding away from zero at the domain endpoint pushes the result OVER the bound.

CONCRETE FAILING INPUT — written and run by me with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file> --run:

       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ADVRV01.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> 1.57079632679489662 is pi/2 rounded UP at 17 fraction digits,
      *> so it is >= the true pi/2.
       01 HALFPI  PIC S9V9(17) VALUE 1.57079632679489662.
       01 NHALFPI PIC S9V9(17) VALUE -1.57079632679489662.
       01 R       PIC S9V9(9).
       01 R17     PIC S9V9(17).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           DISPLAY "ASIN1  = " R
           IF R > HALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION: ASIN(1) > PI/2" END-IF
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ASIN(-1)
           DISPLAY "ASINM1 = " R
           IF R < NHALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION: ASIN(-1) < -PI/2" END-IF
           COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           DISPLAY "ASIN1-17 = " R17
           IF R17 > HALFPI DISPLAY "VIOLATION17: ASIN(1) > PI/2" END-IF
           DISPLAY "DIRECT: " FUNCTION ASIN(1)
           STOP RUN.

ACTUAL OUTPUT (verbatim; the trailing letter is the signed-DISPLAY overpunch — G = +7, P = -7, D = +4):
    ASIN1  = 157079632G           -> +1.570796327, over pi/2 by ~2.05e-10
    VIOLATION: ASIN(1) > PI/2
    ASINM1 = 157079632P           -> -1.570796327
    VIOLATION: ASIN(-1) < -PI/2
    ASIN1-17 = 15707963267948966D -> +1.57079632679489664, still over pi/2
    VIOLATION17: ASIN(1) > PI/2
    DIRECT: 1.570796327

The scale-17 line matters: the breach is NOT a 9-digit artifact. At ws=17 the "d * 1e17" product rounds up to 157079632679489664, so widening the working scale does not fix it. The repair has to be at the quantization, not at the precision.

BOUNDARY OF THE DEFECT (checked, so the fix is aimed correctly): RenderFloat's other branch, "num.Receiver.Real ? new NumX(call, 0, Real: true)", bypasses FromDouble entirely, so a COMP-2 receiver keeps the conforming binary64 1.5707963267948966 and does NOT breach. The defect is exactly the fixed-point-receiver path.

PATTERN SWEEP (CLAUDE.md rule 4 — context for the fix, deliberately NOT extra records): the defect lives in the shared quantization, so every §15.4.1 float-family function whose returned-value rule states a RANGE is exposed. Confirmed by me in the same session by running it: FUNCTION ACOS(-1) yields 3.141592654, which exceeds pi = 3.14159265358979, against §15.8.4 r1 "greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to π". §15.11.4 r1 (ATAN — a STRICT "less than +π/2", so even more exposed) and §15.75.4 r1 (RANDOM, 0 <= r < 1) sit on the same round-up. The structural repair is a per-catalog-row returned-value range carried into the ONE FromDouble quantization site (clamp, or round toward zero at a stated endpoint), not a hand-written clamp per runtime body — a hand-maintained list where a structure belongs is what CLAUDE.md rule 5 forbids.

EDITIONS, ESTABLISHED FROM THE SPEC AND NOT FROM IntrinsicCatalog's ROW: ASIN occurs in specs/ISO_COBOL.md only in the table of contents, the index, §8.11 Intrinsic function names, the §15.6 summary table and §15.10 itself; it appears in NO Annex E added/changed list, so the returned-value rule is unchanged across the editions this compiler models. Caveat recorded: intrinsic functions reached the 85 line via the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment rather than base ISO 1989:1985; on this compiler's modelling of --std 85 the rule applies to all four, and I confirmed all four editions produce identical values.

COVERAGE: no spec-derived test. A grep of tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance and tests/conformance restricted to *.cs/*.cob/*.json finds no ASIN case at all; the frozen legacy tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Runtime/IntrinsicFunctionTests.cs#Asin_ViaDispatch and the NIST goldens IF103A/IF401M cannot close the row. The test this row needs is an ENDPOINT test (ASIN(1) and ASIN(-1)) with the bound computed from §15.10.4 — note that a test written only at ASIN(0.5) would pass today and pin the defect open.

subject: ATAN function
notes:
SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS: verdict SURVIVES. Independently reproduced, and the ONE escape reading that could have rescued a CONFORMS is now closed by a receiver-free repro rather than by argument. Two factual errors in the prior record's CAUSE paragraph are corrected below — both would have misdirected the fix.

CITATION re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.11.4 "greater than"` => OK  §15.11.4 1). Confirmed against the PRINTED page (render-spec-page.py 850, folio 820): "The returned value is the approximation of the arctangent of argument-1 and is greater than −π/2 and less than +π/2." One rule, two halves — BOTH checked below.

THE BOUND IS NORMATIVE, chain re-derived from the spec text and each link validated. §15.4 (`cite.py --check 15.4 "temporary elementary data item"` => OK): "The evaluation of a function produces a returned value in a temporary elementary data item" — the returned value IS what that temporary holds. §15.4.1 (`cite.py --check 15.4.1 "unless otherwise specified in the function definition"` => OK): "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED in the function definition." ATAN has no equivalent arithmetic expression and §15.11.4 IS that otherwise-specification. That the interval is deliberate is confirmed by the neighbour: `cite.py --check 15.10.4 "greater than or equal to"` => OK — ASIN gets a CLOSED interval where ATAN gets an OPEN one.

HALF ONE (the approximation) IS CORRECT — verified, so this is a genuine one-sided defect and not an unexamined edge. Re-run: ATAN(1)=00078539816C (+0.785398163 = π/4, radians per §15.11.1), ATAN(-1)=00078539816L (−0.785398163), ATAN(0)=00000000000{, ATAN(0.5)=00046364760I (+0.463647609) both as a literal and as a PIC S9V9(9) item.

HALF TWO (the bound) FAILS, BOTH SIGNS — re-run by this reviewer, default --std 2023, exit 0, R PIC S9(3)V9(9):
  COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000).  => R=00157079632G  (overpunch G = 7+, i.e. +1.570796327 > +π/2 = 1.5707963267948966...)
  COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(-4000000000). => R=00157079632P  (overpunch P = 7−, i.e. −1.570796327 < −π/2)
Threshold measured, not estimated: ATAN(3392000000) => ...G (out of bound), ATAN(3000000000) and ATAN(2000000000) => ...F (+1.570796326, the largest scale-9 value INSIDE the interval, which is what a conforming implementation should return). An ordinary 10-digit argument suffices; this is not an exotic input.

ESCAPE READING CLOSED BY A RECEIVER-FREE REPRO (new this pass, and the reason a CONFORMS is not available). The only serious defence is: "§15.4.1 lets the implementor define the characteristics of the temporary under native arithmetic; our temporary is the binary64 double (in bounds) and the scale-9 value is a STORE artifact." It does not hold — with NO receiver at all, the function-identifier's own temporary is out of bounds. §15.4.1 NOTE 2 makes a relation on a function-identifier the standard's own probe of the returned value. All four of these DISPLAYs fired:

       01 P9 PIC S9V9(9) VALUE 1.570796326.
       ...
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) > P9        *> GT-LARGEST-INBOUND-SCALE9
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) = 1.570796327          *> EQ, out of bound
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(-4000000000) = -1.570796327        *> EQ, out of bound
           IF FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) > 1.570796326795       *> fired

The fourth is decisive: atan(4e9) = 1.5707963265448966 is LESS than 1.570796326795, so a binary64 temporary would make it FALSE. It fired, proving the materialized temporary in a relation is the scale-9 quantized 1.570796327 — quantization happens while PRODUCING the value, not while storing it.

CAUSE, read in the code — TWO CORRECTIONS to the prior record. `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat` computes `int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)` and, when the receiver is not real, wraps the call in FromDouble at ws; in a relation condition Receiver.Scale contributes nothing, so ws = 9 (the fourth probe above proves it — the prior record's "ws = 10 from the comparand" reasoning was wrong). `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble` ends `return (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);` — the cast is **Int128**, not `long` as the prior record wrote. ⛔ AND THE MIDPOINT MODE IS NOT THE CULPRIT: atan(4e9) x 1e9 = 1570796326.5448966, whose fraction is .5449, not a midpoint — EVERY round-to-nearest mode rounds it up. Changing MidpointRounding would NOT fix this; the defect is round-to-NEAREST at the quantization step having no knowledge of the function's declared open bound. `CobolIntrinsics.Float.Atan` is `Math.Atan(x)` and is itself fine (Math.Atan never returns a double outside the interval). All three symbols verified literally present.

CONFORMING PATH, re-run and confirmed: `01 D USAGE COMP-2. COMPUTE D = FUNCTION ATAN(1000000000000).` prints 1.5707963267938967, because RenderFloat returns `new NumX(call, 0, Real: true)` and skips FromDouble when num.Receiver.Real. So the defect is exactly the fixed-point quantization path.

FIX SHAPE: clamp the ATAN quantization to the largest value strictly inside (−π/2, +π/2) at the working scale — equivalently, round toward zero when the magnitude would land on or beyond the scale-ws representation of π/2. NOT a global switch to truncation: FromDouble's hazard-H2 comment records why round-to-nearest is right for the rest of the family (truncation turns LOG10(1000) = 2.9999999999999996 into 2.999999999). The bounded-range siblings ACOS (§15.8.4) and ASIN (§15.10.4) need the same audit; their CLOSED intervals make them a different and possibly non-defective case, so each needs its own rule read rather than a copied fix.

HARDENED AGAINST THE OTHER READING. If "π" meant the implementor's own approximation rather than exact π, the finding still stands: π/2 rounded to scale 9 is itself 1.570796327, so the returned value would then EQUAL the implementor's +π/2 and "less than" still fails. There is no reading of §15.11.4 r1 under which 1.570796327 at scale 9 is admissible.

EDITIONS: as for the other two rows — Annex E.2 item 13's list of names new in 2023 does not include ATAN, establishing 2014 and 2023; §15.11.4 carries no edition qualification and Annex E records no ATAN change; the 85/2002 boundary is not establishable from this document, so all four per the brief's fallback, NOT from IntrinsicCatalog's MinEdition column.

The covering test must assert the BOUND at a large argument (e.g. FUNCTION ATAN(4000000000) < the scale-9 representation of π/2), expected value computed from §15.11.4 r1.

subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2. The DIVERGES verdict is UPHELD - I reproduced both previously-reported divergences myself on the built CLI - but the RECORD IS CORRECTED: the prior adjudication wrongly pushed a THIRD site of the same defect out of scope, and that site is an UNHANDLED RUNTIME CRASH on legal COBOL. Every citation below re-validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check (§15.13.4 r1, §15.13.1, §15.2 item 2, §15.4, §8.8.1.1, §8.8.4.2.8, §8.3.3.3.2 all resolve to the quoted text).

DIVERGENCE 1 - SILENT WRONG BIT CONFIGURATION FOR ANY argument-1 >= 2^63. §15.13.4 r1: the returned value 'has the same bit configuration as the binary representation of the value of argument-1'. §8.3.3.3.2 ('The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals ... 31 digits', verified) and this compiler's own Int128 numeric channel make a 19-25 digit positive integer argument legal COBOL it otherwise handles correctly. MY OWN RUN (--std 2023, PIC 9(25) source items, argument-2 = 70 so the §15.13.4 left-truncation clause cannot apply): 2^62 -> correct; 2^63-1 -> correct (63 one-bits); 2^63 (9223372036854775808) -> SEVENTY ZEROS, required is 6 zeros then '1' then 63 zeros; 2^64+5 (18446744073709551621) -> '...000101' with the 2^64 bit SILENTLY DROPPED. No exception, no diagnostic - the cliff is exactly at 2^63. §15.4's implementor-maximum escape does not cover it: §15.4 scopes that maximum to 'the length of the returned value', and the returned length here is 70, far under this compiler's own documented 8191 cap; §15.13.3 r1 is satisfied (the argument IS a positive integer), so EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION does not cover it either. ROOT CAUSE, read in the generated C# (m1.g.cs): IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt renders EVERY integer-kind intrinsic argument as an unchecked truncating '(long)(...)' cast - the emitted line is literally 'CobolIntrinsics.BooleanOfInteger((long)(V63), (long)(70L))' where V63 is an Int128 - and the runtime body CobolIntrinsics.BooleanOfInteger(long value, long length) additionally caps its bit loop at 'i < 63'. BOTH sites must widen; widening one leaves the other as the cliff. AsInt is the SHARED integer-argument bridge, so every sibling integer-argument intrinsic needs the same sweep.

DIVERGENCE 2 - THE RESULT IS NOT OF CLASS/CATEGORY BOOLEAN. §15.13.4 r1 first sentence: 'The returned value is a boolean item of usage bit'; §15.13.1 'The function type is boolean'; §15.2 item 2 'Boolean functions. These are of the class and category boolean. Boolean functions have an implicit usage bit', plus §15.2's 'the function so described may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified'; §8.8.4.2.8 'An operand of class boolean may be compared with another operand of class boolean'. REPRODUCED BY ME at --std 2023 (the prior report states the same at 2002/2014): (i) 'IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(544, 6) = B"100000"' -> error COBOLNET0844 'a boolean operand may be compared only with another boolean operand or the figurative constant ZERO'; (ii) 'COMPUTE B8 = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) B-AND B"00001111"' -> error COBOLNET1511 'is not a valid boolean operand'. AND THE MIRROR, also reproduced: 'IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) = "00000101"' is ACCEPTED and evaluates TRUE, an alphanumeric relation over a class-boolean operand that COBOLNET0844's own message text cites §8.8.4.2.1 F1 SR2/SR3 as excluding. The divergence is bidirectional - legal boolean uses rejected, illegal alphanumeric uses accepted - because the result silently carries the alphanumeric '0'/'1' substrate. Also reproduced: 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) + 1' binds clean and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException('string-class FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER in a numeric context') at RUN time, where §8.8.1.1 ('An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal, the figurative constant ZERO ...', verified) makes it a compile-time error.

DIVERGENCE 3 - NEW IN THIS PASS; THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION WRONGLY FILED IT AS 'a §15.50 row, not §15.13.4'. THAT DISMISSAL IS WRONG, and I disproved it with a control run. §15.13.4 r1's SECOND sentence is 'in order to return a boolean item whose length is specified by argument-2 in terms of boolean positions'; §15.50.4 r1 makes FUNCTION LENGTH over an elementary boolean data item return that length in boolean positions, and §15.50.3 r1 admits 'a data item of any class or category'. MY RUN, one program, --std 2023: 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abcdef"))' prints LEN-UC=0006 (a nested ALPHANUMERIC intrinsic works), while the very next statement 'COMPUTE N = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8))' - required value 8 - dies with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException('FUNCTION LENGTH argument (a numeric/figurative literal is not a valid argument, ISO 15.50.3)'). It is therefore NOT a generic §15.50 gap; it is specific to the BOOLEAN result and is the same root cause as divergence 2. NAMED SITE: in IntrinsicBinder.cs, BOTH BindLengthFold and IsStringOperand carry the nested-intrinsic pattern 'BoundComputedOperand { Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall { ResultCategory: PicCategory.Alphanumeric or PicCategory.National } }' - Boolean is absent from the list in both, so a boolean function result falls into the '_' error arm. Note IsStringOperand's BoundFieldOperand arm DOES include PicCategory.Boolean: the same rule is written twice and the second copy forgot boolean.

COMMON ROOT CAUSE (one rule, four places). IntrinsicCatalog.ResultCategory correctly maps IntrinsicType.Boolean -> PicCategory.Boolean, and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is the ONLY IntrinsicType.Boolean row in the catalog. That single fact is then never read at the class-boolean checkpoints: StatementValidation.CheckRelationalOperands (whose local IsBoolOperand and BoolCompatible are themselves the same predicate written twice), ConditionBinder.BindBoolOperandValue, IntrinsicBinder.BindLengthFold and IntrinsicBinder.IsStringOperand. None has an arm for a BoundComputedOperand wrapping a BoundIntrinsicCall whose ResultCategory is Boolean - which is exactly what a function-identifier binds to. The fix is the extraction (one predicate answering 'is this operand class boolean', consulted at all four sites), not four patches.

WHAT IS CORRECT: the rightmost-is-low-order ordering, the left zero-fill, the left truncation (2^70 over 70 positions -> all zeros IS correct, since 2^70 mod 2^70 = 0 - I checked this before calling anything a defect), and the returned length being argument-2 including a RUNTIME argument-2 ('DISPLAY FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, LN)' with LN=12 prints 12 positions).

TEST-REF: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob (+ .out) exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, is spec-derived (values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example; not characterization/nist/legacy), and I re-ran it - it reproduces its golden. It covers the ordering, zero-fill and truncation halves FOR SMALL VALUES ONLY, and it would stay GREEN through all three divergences. test-needed for all three: nothing covers argument-1 >= 2^63; nothing covers the class-boolean half (every existing case MOVEs the result into a PIC 1(n) BIT item first, which is exactly why the defects survived); nothing covers FUNCTION LENGTH over the result.

EDITIONS derived as for FMT-15.13.2 - Annex E (2014 -> 2023 substantive changes) does not mention the function, and the 85 exclusion is external knowledge (boolean data is a COBOL-2002 addition) rather than a spec quotation - NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE, no record added (no AR rule for this function was in my input, and I verified these are not §15.13.4 issues): BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, so §15.13.3 r1/r2 remain UNSCREENED by the PB1 §15.3 class screen; and the FUNCTION-omitted form without a REPOSITORY entry is undiagnosed at bind, which I confirmed is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap (an undefined user name and UPPER-CASE behave identically), not this function's.

WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 BB PIC 1(5) USAGE BIT. 01 BGRP. 05 C1 PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT. 05 C2 PIC 1(2) USAGE BIT. 01 BD PIC 1(5). PROCEDURE DIVISION. DISPLAY "BB=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(BB). notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified by running — the worst finding in this batch, a SILENT wrong value with no diagnostic and no loud stage. A variable-length group (§8.5.1.12.1, cite.py OK: 'a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item') folds to a compile-time constant that omits exactly the variable part. §15.3 permits it as an argument ('A variable-length group shall be referenced as an argument to a function only when explicitly permitted in the function definition' — §15.14.4 r6/r7 explicitly permit it). Failing input, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVVLG01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 VLG. 05 F1 PIC X(4). 05 DL PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH. 01 DCG. 05 F2 PIC X(2). 05 DT OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP PIC X(3). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE "HELLO" TO DL DISPLAY "LEN-DL=" FUNCTION LENGTH(DL). DISPLAY "BL-VLG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(VLG). DISPLAY "CAP=" CAP. DISPLAY "BL-DCG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(DCG). STOP RUN.` -> prints LEN-DL=5, BL-VLG=4, CAP=0000000000, BL-DCG=5. BYTE-LENGTH(DCG) at capacity 0 = r6 a) 2 + r6 c) 0 = 2, COBOL.NET says 5 (ByteWidth multiplies the dynamic table by `c.Occurs ?? 1`, one phantom element). A SECOND run confirms the constant never tracks capacity: after `MOVE "AAA" TO DT(4)` the program prints CAP=0000000004 and BL-DCG=5, where r6 c) requires 2 + 4 x 3 = 14. subject: CHAR function
notes: test-needed. UPHELD by adversarial re-review; code-location EXTENDED to name DataBinder.Switches.cs#AlphabetBind, which is where the defect's root (the 256-entry domain) is built and where the fix belongs. §15.3's closing paragraph (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29556) makes this a runtime rule: an incorrect argument value sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, and 'if checking ... is not enabled, the implementor defines the result'. Measured: CHAR(0), CHAR(-3) and CHAR(65537) all yield the §15.3 one-space default, CHAR(65536) round-trips through ORD to 65536, and with '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' CHAR(0) aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)'. NON-IDENTITY-PCS HALF IS WRONG AT BOTH ENDS. Char(long, ushort[]) receives the 256-entry table AlphabetBind builds ('var pos = new ushort[256]') and treats positions 0..weights.Length-1 as always occupied; an ALSO phrase COLLAPSES positions, so the top of the Latin-1 block goes empty and the >Latin-1 tail shifts down. Re-ran at --std 2023 and --std 85, identical: OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B". 01 N PIC 9(6). MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(255)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD255=" N. MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(65536)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD65536=" N. -> ORD255=000034 and ORD65536=065534. Therefore ordinal 255 IS in range (position 254 = code 256 = U+0100) yet CHAR(255) raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and returns the one-space default (ORD of a space under this alphabet is 34: space = code 32, unspecified codes 0..64 take positions 1..65, so space is at position 33, ordinal 34 — matches the measured 000034); and ordinal 65536 is OUT of range (max is 65534) yet is accepted, returning U+FFFF, whose true ordinal is 65534 — the out-of-range value is not merely accepted, it ALIASES a legal one and is indistinguishable from it. ALSO ACTIONABLE: both ArgumentError messages in Char cite '§15.15.3 rule 1' when the rule actually violated is r2 (the range rule); r1 is the integer rule. TEST-REF STRUCK AND RE-VERIFIED STRUCK: tests/conformance/2002/ca26_char_unicode_pcs.cob (read in full) shows only two IN-RANGE ordinals (256, 257) under a bijective 26-letter permutation alphabet; it never uses an ALSO phrase and never probes 0, a negative or an above-maximum ordinal, so it cannot cover this rule.

Both bodies read side by side: Char(long, ushort[]) still has 'if (wanted >= weights.Length && wanted <= 0xFFFF) return ((char)wanted).ToString();' — a position past the 256-entry table falls back to its NATIVE code unit. Ord(string, ushort[]) no longer does: it computes 'highest + 1L + (c - weights.Length) + 1L' with a remark documenting the removed fallback ('a character one past the table was numbered by a different rule than its neighbour and left a HOLE'). The two are inverses only while the table is a bijection over 0..255; any ALSO phrase collapses positions and they disagree. Re-ran at --std 2023 and --std 85, identical output both: OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B". 01 N PIC 9(6). MOVE FUNCTION ORD(FUNCTION CHAR(255)) TO N. DISPLAY "ORD255=" N. CHAR(255) shall be U+0100 but returns the one-space EC default; CHAR(257) shall be U+0102 but returns U+0100. ORD is the half that is RIGHT here — ORD(U+0100) = 253+1+0+1 = 255 agrees with the spec derivation — so the fix belongs in Char, mirroring Ord's arithmetic, not the reverse. TEST-REF KEPT, RE-VERIFIED ON DISK AND RE-DERIVED: tests/conformance/2002/ca26_char_unicode_pcs.cob exists with its .out, and its expected values are COMPUTED from the standard rather than captured — I recomputed them independently: under ALPHABET AL IS "ZYXWVUTSRQPONMLKJIHGFEDCBA", Z..A occupy positions 0..25, the 230 unspecified Latin-1 code units occupy 26..255 (so CHAR(256) = X"FF"), and code 256 = U+0100 sits at position 256 = ordinal 257, which is exactly the golden's 'ORD=00257' and 'P-GT-R'. It genuinely exercises this rule under a non-identity PCS, but only over a BIJECTIVE alphabet with NO ALSO phrase — precisely the case the defect cannot reach — so it does not close the row and an ALSO variant is still needed. (Note for whoever lands the fix: that fixture's header comment cites '§12.3.7 k)3', the one-level-short form; the clause that actually carries the rule is §12.3.7.4 GR7 1.3.)

notes:
OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. The bound check is real but it sits DOWNSTREAM OF A LOSSY NARROWING, so it can be walked straight past. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits '(long)({a.Expr})' over an Int128-typed argument expression; the C# Int128->long conversion is UNCHECKED and wraps modulo 2^64. An argument value of magnitude >= 2^63 therefore ALIASES into the valid 1..65536 window before CobolIntrinsics.CharNational's 'if (c is < 0 or > 0xFFFF)' ever sees it, and §15.16.3 rule 2 is violated with no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION at all.
PREMISE VALIDATED (not just the rule): §8.3.3.3.2 — 'The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length' and 'An integer literal is a fixed-point numeric literal that contains no decimal point'. A 20-digit unsigned integer literal, and a PIC 9(20) item holding it, are both legal and both satisfy §15.16.3 rule 1 — so this is a pure rule-2 violation, not a rule-1 one. §15.3 (validated with cite.py) then requires: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' It is not set.
RAN, with checking explicitly ENABLED so the §15.3 implementor-defined-result latitude cannot excuse it — exit 0, no diagnostic, no exception, execution continues past the call:
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ADVCN15.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  N-CHAR   PIC N(1) USAGE NATIONAL.
       01  A-DISP   PIC X(1).
       01  BIGN     PIC 9(20) VALUE 18446744073709551682.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (BIGN) TO N-CHAR
           MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF (N-CHAR) TO A-DISP
           DISPLAY "ITEM-2POW64PLUS66=[" A-DISP "]"
           DISPLAY "NOT-RAISED"
           STOP RUN.
prints 'ITEM-2POW64PLUS66=[A]' then 'NOT-RAISED'. 18446744073709551682 = 2^64 + 66, so the wrap delivers 66 and the function answers with ordinal 66's character. Identical result for the LITERAL form 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (18446744073709551682)', and identical at --std 2002 and --std 2023.
CONTROL that isolates the wrap as the cause: 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (9223372036854775807)' (long.MaxValue — one below the wrap threshold, no aliasing) DOES abort correctly with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): CHAR-NATIONAL argument 9223372036854775807 outside the national collating sequence', exit 1. Same rule, same statement shape, opposite outcome, and the only difference is whether the value survives the (long) cast.
WHAT DOES WORK (read and run, so the fix is narrow): identity path rejects n<1 and n>65536 (ran n=0 -> space with checking off, fatal EC with checking on; n=65536 accepted, n=70000 rejected). Non-native path routes through NationalCollation.CharAt, bounded by PositionCount = NextFree + (0x10000 - |specified codes|), which correctly SHRINKS under ALSO — ran 'ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C"' with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL: ordinal 65535 accepted, 65536 rejected. So the DEFECT IS THE ARGUMENT CHANNEL, not the bound.
FIX (root cause, CLAUDE.md rule 4): ArgInt/IntArg must not silently narrow. Either render a checked/saturating conversion, or carry the argument as Int128 to the runtime and let the runtime's own range test see the true value. This is a WHOLE-CHANNEL defect, not a CHAR-NATIONAL one — every 'i' argument rendered through AsInt has it (CHAR §15.15.3, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER §15.13.3, BASE-CONVERT §15.12.3, FORMATTED-DATE/-TIME/-DATETIME offsets, the DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD / DAY-TO-YYYYDDD / YEAR-TO-YYYY windowing trio); sweep them together.

subject: COMBINED-DATETIME function
notes: VERDICT RETAINED, NOTES OVERTURNED - the prior record's root cause and BOTH of its failing inputs are FALSE against the current tree, and a fixer sent to them would find nothing. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.17.4 "equivalent arithmetic expression"` -> OK. REFUTED CLAIM 1: 'CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble returns a long and saturates at 9.2e18'. It does not. Read it: `public static Int128 FromDouble(double d, int scale)` with `if (scaled >= 1.7e38) return Int128.MaxValue;`. REFUTED CLAIM 2: `COMPUTE <PIC 9(9)V9(14)> = FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(143951, <COMP-2 18867.8125>)` was said to print 92233.72036854775807. RE-RAN it: it prints `F14=00014395118867812501504` (= 143951.18867812501504). REFUTED CLAIM 3 (its collateral repro): `COMPUTE <PIC 9(9)V9(17)> = FUNCTION SQRT(20000000)` was said to print long.MaxValue. RE-RAN: `SQ=00000447213595499957977088` (= 4472.13595499957977088, correct). There is no saturation anywhere in this family at reachable magnitudes. EXACT LEG - CONFORMS, re-verified: `CombinedDatetime(long integerDate, Int128 secUnscaled, int secScale) => (Int128)integerDate * Pow10.AsWide(secScale + 5) + secUnscaled`, read by RenderNum at scale secScale+5, which is algebraically a1 + a2/100000 with no rounding. Battery re-run at --std 2023, every value exact: scale-12 argument-2 18867.812479168304 into PIC Z(6)9.9(17) -> `143951.18867812479168304`, bit-for-bit the standard's own worked value in D.31.5.11; literal arguments -> 143951.45296; argument-2 = 1 -> 143951.00001; COMP-3 45296.125 -> 143951.45296125; the expression form (WS-ID + 1, WS-SEC / 2) -> 143952.22648; argument-2 = 0.5 -> 143951.000005. Under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` it is exact and the §15.4.1 NOTE 2 relation holds (`IF FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-S12) = WS-ID + (WS-S12 / 100000)` prints EAE-EQUAL). FLOATING-POINT LEG - THE REAL DEFECT, correctly attributed this time. A COMP-2 argument-2 is legal (§15.6 types it Num2) and routes through `RenderNum`'s `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(...)` to `CombinedDatetimeReal`, whose expression is right. But `RenderFloat` quantizes at `int ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9)`, and on the MOVE path `num.Receiver.Scale` is not the MOVE's receiver, so the float leg quantizes at 9 regardless of what the receiver holds. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` at --std 2023: `01 WS-ID PIC 9(7) VALUE 143951. 01 WS-SEC USAGE COMP-2. 01 WS-13 PIC 9(9)V9(13). 01 WS-13B PIC 9(9)V9(13). MOVE 18867.812479168304 TO WS-SEC. MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-13. COMPUTE WS-13B = FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC). COMPUTE WS-13B = WS-ID + (WS-SEC / 100000).` prints `MOVE13=0001439511886781250000`, `COMP13=0001439511886781248000`, `EAE13 =0001439511886781247916` - i.e. the SAME function reference with the SAME arguments returns TWO DIFFERENT values in one execution, and neither equals the equivalent arithmetic expression. That violates §15.4.1's standard-arithmetic paragraph (cite.py --check 15.4.1 "same for all instances of a given function" -> OK): 'the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element so long as the value and order of the arguments, the collating sequence, and the locale are unchanged' - COMBINED-DATETIME is not one of the four excepted functions (DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, RANDOM, YEAR-TO-YYYY) - and the same paragraph's rule 1, 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'. Under NATIVE arithmetic the same divergence is defensible, because §15.4.1 there permits 'an implementor-defined approximation'; under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is not. ROOT CAUSE IS SHARED, not this function's body: it is the same `FromDouble(call, ws)` fixed-point RECEIVER path already recorded PARTIAL for RANDOM in docs/rearchitecture/CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE.md. PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS because a legal program gets two different answers for one function reference; PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because the exact leg - which is what §15.17.4 r1 and the standard's own worked example exercise - is bit-exact. TEST: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob with golden `CDT= 153569.45296` = 153569 + 45296/100000 computed from §15.17.4 r1 (file and .out read on disk) covers the EXACT leg only; test-needed for the floating-point leg and for the standard-arithmetic 'same for all instances' invariant. subject: CONCAT function
notes: 'StrArgList(ic) => string.Join(", ", ic.Args.Select(Str))' renders every argument in SOURCE ORDER into one 'Concat(params string[] parts) => string.Concat(parts)' call, a left-to-right fold — the iterated form §15.18.4 r4 prescribes (each concatenation's result becomes argument-1 of the next iteration). subject: CONVERT function
notes:

Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "The source-format shall be different from the destination-format" -> OK, rule 3). The source-format space is {ANY, ANUM, HEX, NAT} and the destination space is {ANUM, ANUM HEX, NAT, NAT HEX, BYTE}, so the only pairs that can be the SAME format are ANUM->ANUM and NAT->NAT with no HEX - which is exactly `(src==1 && dst==1 && !hex) || (src==3 && dst==3 && !hex)`. subject: CONVERT function
notes:

(a) 'valid string of hexadecimal digits ... representing complete bytes' is enforced at RUNTIME in HexDigitsToBytes: an odd digit count and a non-hex digit each call ExceptionState.ArgumentError (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION). HOLE: the method opens with `string t = s.Trim()`, so spaces are DISCARDED rather than diagnosed. Re-ran: `01 WS-LEAD PIC X(4) VALUE "  41".` / CONVERT(WS-LEAD HEX BYTE) -> "A" with no exception, and `01 WS-BLANK PIC X(4) VALUE SPACES.` / CONVERT(WS-BLANK HEX BYTE) -> empty, again with no exception. The trim is needed for the fixed-width image, so the fix is a trailing-image trim plus a digits-only screen, not deleting the trim.
(b) 'of display or national usage' is NOWHERE enforced - nothing inspects argument-1's USAGE. Re-ran:
       01 WS-N9 PIC 9(4) BINARY VALUE 4142.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-N9 HEX ANUM) TO WS-R.
-> R4=[AB]. A BINARY item is neither display nor national usage, so 15.19.3 rule 4 makes it an illegal HEX source and 15.3 rule 14 (validated) requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION; the compiler silently converts its display image instead.
ALSO RE-RUN: 15.19.4 NOTE 3 b as literally written, FUNCTION CONVERT (X"41" HEX ANUM), returns U+00A0 here (re-hexed: A0), not "A". That is DEFENSIBLE - X"41" is the one character 'A', i.e. a single hex digit, which rule 4 forbids as not 'complete bytes', so the compiler takes the odd-count path and pads; the NOTE's literal form is self-inconsistent and must NOT become a golden. subject: CONVERT function
notes:

SUSTAINED - I re-read IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified line by line and CONVERT is genuinely absent from it (the dictionary holds ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI and nothing else), so the PB1 15.3 class screen never runs for CONVERT; and BindConvert performs no class, category or repertoire check on argument-1 - only zero-length-literal, the format-pair shape, SR3, SR8 and SR9. Two failing inputs, both re-run:
(1) a class-numeric BINARY item accepted as an ANUM source:
       01 WS-N9 PIC 9(4) BINARY VALUE 4142.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-N9 ANUM ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> R5=[34313432] - the hex of the CHARACTERS "4142". A BINARY item is not 'a valid string of characters from the program's alphanumeric coded character set'; 15.3 rule 14 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION.
(2) a character outside the set CONVERT's own byte model assumes, silently corrupted instead of diagnosed:

           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-X ANUM ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> XHEX=[413F4220]: the U+0160 position came back as 3F ('?'). I confirmed the item really does hold U+0160 - FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) returns 353 (= 352 + 1). It does neither.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:

(a) The EXCLUSION LIST is unenforced - nothing rejects an index, message-tag, object-reference, pointer, function-pointer or program-pointer argument-1 under ANY.
(b) 'It is not necessary for the contents to be valid according to the usage' means ANY reads the item's RAW STORAGE (15.19.1: 'the representation of most types of data item in hexadecimal'). The implementation passes the operand's DISPLAY IMAGE instead: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderString emits `CobolIntrinsics.Convert(Str(ic.Args[0]), {ic.ConvertSource}, {ic.ConvertDest}, ...)` - Str() is the display-image channel - and BindConvert's only concession is re-tagging ANY as NAT when the operand is national (`int runtimeSrc = src == 0 && IsNationalOperand(operands[0]) ? 3 : src;`).
Re-run verbatim:
       01 WS-PTR USAGE POINTER.  01 WS-IDX USAGE INDEX.  01 WS-B PIC S9(4) BINARY VALUE 1.
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-PTR ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> PTR=[436F626F6C4E65742E52756E74696D65]
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-IDX ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> IDX=[] (empty)
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-B   ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.  *> BIN=[30303031]

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED at PARTIAL. The VALUE half conforms on both reachable sources (rule 8 bars ANY and rule 3 bars ANUM, so a bare-ANUM destination comes only from NAT or HEX): NAT->ANUM routes to the ONE shared Repertoire translator, HEX->ANUM emits one alphanumeric position per byte (verified CONVERT("41" HEX ANUM) = "A"). The SUBSTITUTION half does not close, for two reasons.
(a) ABSENT ON THE HEX->ANUM PATH. That path is `chars[i] = (char)bytes[i]` with no validity test of any kind, making it byte-for-byte identical to the BYTE destination (rule 5) - yet rule 1 and rule 5 differ PRECISELY in that rule 1 carries a coded-character-set screen and rule 5 does not.
(b) THE HALF THAT IS PRESENT RESTS ON A CHARACTER SET THE COMPILER CONTRADICTS ELSEWHERE. Repertoire substitutes when `c > 0xFF` (`sb.Append(toNational || c <= 0xFF ? c : sub ?? Sub())`), i.e. rule 1's 'valid set of characters from the alphanumeric coded character set' is read as Latin-1. But a PIC X item in this compiler demonstrably holds U+0160: `01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE "A<U+0160>B".` / FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) returns 353 - I re-ran this myself - and the project's stated alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16. If the alphanumeric coded set is UTF-16, rule 1 must return U+0160 unchanged and must NOT set EC-DATA-CONVERSION, and the cited test is pinning the wrong answer; if it is Latin-1, then (a) is a real gap AND a PIC X item may not hold U+0160 at all. Exactly one of the two is wrong under either reading, and choosing between them is an implementor-defined-set decision the project has not written down in one place.
Mechanics that DO check out and that I re-verified rather than assuming: Sub() returns the implementor-defined '?' AND calls ExceptionState.DataConversionError, and BOTH effects are observable - CONVERT(N"A<U+0160>" NAT ANUM) yields "A?" and the cited test asserts EXCEPTION-STATUS = EC-DATA-CONVERSION. Test-ref audited and KEPT (a plain CompileAndRun with a hardcoded spec-derived expectation, not a legacy comparison), but it covers only the contested half.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL TO DIVERGES. The prior verdict treated the second half as merely 'unimplemented', but I RAN two inputs that each return a value WRONG under rule 2's own normative text, so this is demonstrated divergence, not an unverified edge. Citation validated (--check 15.19.4 "the trailing portion needed to make up a complete multiple is padded with zero bits" -> OK, rule 2).
(a) CONFORMS: 'a string of hexadecimal digits in display format' for all three legal character sources (ANUM "A" -> "41" = NOTE 3 a; ANUM "AB " -> "414220"; NAT N"A" -> "0041" over UTF-16BE), spec-tested by the cited theory.
(b) DIVERGES - the ZERO-BIT PADDING clause. CobolIntrinsics.Convert reduces argument-1 to a byte[] built from CHARACTERS (one byte per code unit for ANUM/ANY, two for NAT) and has NO sub-byte path, so an argument whose bit count is not a multiple of 8 is never padded. Re-run:
       01 ITEM-B PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(ITEM-B ANY ANUM HEX) TO WS-R.
-> BITANUM=[313031], the hex of the CHARACTERS "101". Rule 2's own arithmetic (an alphanumeric character being 8 bits in this implementation) gives 101 + five zero bits = 1010 0000 = "A0". 313031 is wrong under every reading of the clause. NOTE: do NOT carry "E0" from NOTE 3 c into an ANUM-HEX golden - 1010 0000 is 0xA0, and E0 is not derivable from B"101" under rule 2 at all.
(c) DIVERGES - THE IMPLEMENTED HALF IS LOSSY AND RULE 2 AUTHORIZES NO LOSS. Unlike rules 1 and 3, rule 2 has no substitution clause whatsoever, yet `bytes[i] = arg[i] <= 0xFF ? (byte)arg[i] : ByteSub()` replaces any code unit above 0xFF with 0x3F and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION. Re-run: `01 WS-X PIC X(4) VALUE "A<U+0160>B".` / CONVERT(WS-X ANUM ANUM HEX) -> XHEX=[413F4220], with FUNCTION ORD(WS-X(2:1)) = 353 proving the item really holds U+0160. See RV-15.19.4-1 note (b) - the same unmade character-set decision.
Reachability note for (b): with an ANUM source (8 bits/char), a NAT source (16) or a HEX source (8/byte) the bit count is ALWAYS a multiple of 8, so rule 2's padding clause is reachable only through an ANY source over a sub-byte item - which makes its root cause shared with AR-15.19.3-7 (ANY delivers Str(arg), the display image, not the storage bits).
Test-ref kept for half (a) only; halves (b) and (c) still need spec-derived tests.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED at PARTIAL (deliberately NOT raised to DIVERGES: the only demonstrable failing value depends on a national-character-set definition the project has not fixed, so the missing half is absent rather than provably wrong). TWO HALVES, ONE VERIFIED. The value half conforms on both paths that can reach a bare NAT destination (rule 8 bars ANY, rule 3 bars NAT): ANUM->NAT through Repertoire (identity, the alphanumeric set being a subset of national - covered by the cited round-trip test, which is a plain spec-expectation assertion, not a legacy comparison) and HEX->NAT through the byte pathway (two bytes -> one UTF-16BE code unit, a trailing odd byte zero-filled).
The 'does not correspond to a valid set of national characters -> implementor-defined substitution character + EC-DATA-CONVERSION' half is ABSENT on the HEX->NAT path: Repertoire never substitutes when toNational is true (`sb.Append(toNational || c <= 0xFF ? c : sub ?? Sub())`) and the byte pathway performs no validity check at all. With checking explicitly on:
       01 WS-HX PIC X(4) VALUE "D800".   01 WS-NR PIC N(4).
       >>TURN EC-DATA-CONVERSION CHECKING ON
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-HX HEX NAT) TO WS-NR.
-> FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS all spaces and WS-NR holding the lone surrogate U+D800. Whether an unpaired surrogate is 'not a valid national character' is exactly the implementor-defined decision above; but under ANY definition narrower than 'all 65536 code units' something is invalid, and NOTHING is checked on this path, so the half cannot be closed.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
test-needed - no existing test uses a NAT HEX destination at all (Convert_Formats_2023's national row is NAT -> ANUM HEX). SUSTAINED, and STRENGTHENED with a repro the prior record did not have.
NEW, CLEANER REPRO - the padding defect is NOT confined to the ANY/BIT path, which is what the prior record implied. Rule 4 pads to 'a multiple of those needed for a single NATIONAL character' = 16 bits here (national is UTF-16, two bytes per position, D-N1). An ALPHANUMERIC source of ODD byte length therefore needs padding too. Run:
       01 WS-A  PIC X VALUE "A".   01 WS-NR PIC N(8).
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-A ANUM NAT HEX) TO WS-NR.
-> ANATHEX=[41]. Argument-1 is 8 bits, not a multiple of 16, so rule 4 requires 8 trailing zero bits -> 0x4100 -> "4100". The compiler emits "41". No BIT usage, no ANY source, no reliance on NOTE 3.
ORIGINAL REPRO, re-run: `01 ITEM-B PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101".` / MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(ITEM-B ANY NAT HEX) TO WS-NR -> BITNAT=[313031], the hex of the CHARACTERS "101" rather than of the item's three data bits. Two defects compound there: the ANY source delivers the display image instead of the storage bits (AR-15.19.3-7), and there is no bit-level padding step before ToHex.
WHAT THE EXPECTED VALUE IS NOT: "E0" from 15.19.4 NOTE 3 c must NOT become a golden. Under rule 4's own arithmetic B"101" pads to 1010 0000 0000 0000 = "A000"; "E0" is reachable only by padding to EIGHT bits (rule 2's multiple, not rule 4's) AND reading the value as B"111". The NOTE is wrong on both counts. This DIVERGENCE rests on rule 4's normative text alone.
The digit-CODE-POINT half of the rule ('in national format') IS correct and I re-verified it independently: BindConvert sets `category = dst == 3 ? PicCategory.National : PicCategory.Alphanumeric` per the 15.19.1 table, and CONVERT(WS-N NAT NAT HEX) re-hexed through ANUM HEX gives 0030 0030 0034 0031 - the digits "0041" as national positions.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS TO PARTIAL. Rule 5's own normative SENTENCE conforms - that part of the prior record survives re-checking, and I extended it: rule 9 forces a HEX source, so the rule reduces to hex-digit pairs -> bytes -> one alphanumeric position per byte, which is exactly the fall-through `for (int i = 0; i < bytes.Length; i++) chars[i] = (char)bytes[i];`, with the 15.19.1 Alphanumeric result type (dst == 4 is not 3, so PicCategory.Alphanumeric). Beyond the golden I ran four more edges myself: CONVERT("4142" HEX BYTE) = "AB" (multi-byte), CONVERT("FF" HEX BYTE) -> FUNCTION ORD = 256, i.e. U+00FF (high-byte edge), CONVERT("00" HEX BYTE) -> one U+0000 position (re-hexed: 00), and a NATIONAL-usage hex source `01 WS-NH PIC N(2) VALUE N"41".` -> "A" (which matters because rule 4 admits national hex digits). Citation validated (--check 15.19.4 "the returned value is a string of bytes that represents the value expressed in argument-1" -> OK, rule 5). The cited corpus case exists on disk (tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_convert.cob, `MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(WS-HX HEX BYTE) TO WS-R.`), is listed in the "enabled" array of tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json, and its golden line is `HB=A` - a spec-derived value compared by CorpusRunnerTests, not a recorded oracle.
WHY THE ROW STILL CANNOT BE CLOSED. The rule text carried by this row includes 15.19.4 NOTE 3 and its three worked examples, and two of the three do not reproduce - I ran both:
  - NOTE 3 c, `CONVERT(item-b ANY NAT HEX)` over `PIC 111 USAGE BIT VALUE B"101"`, returns 313031. (Root cause charged on RV-15.19.4-4; listed here because it is part of THIS row's text.)
  - NOTE 3 b as literally written in the BYTE family, `FUNCTION CONVERT (X"41" HEX BYTE)` and `... HEX ANUM`, both return U+00A0, not "A".
And the premise rule 5 depends on - that argument-1 IS 'a valid string of hexadecimal digits ... representing complete bytes' - is only half enforced (AR-15.19.3-4): HexDigitsToBytes silently `Trim()`s, so CONVERT("  41" HEX BYTE) returns "A" and an all-blank source returns an empty byte string, both with no exception. Rule 5 therefore returns a 'string of bytes' for arguments that are not byte strings.
NOTED, not charged here: this implementation makes a BYTE destination byte-for-byte identical to a bare ANUM destination, so the cited golden HB=A would pass even if BYTE were routed through the rule-1 path. Under the compiler's Latin-1 byte model every byte maps to a valid alphanumeric character, so the identity is not itself a defect - but it does mean the golden cannot discriminate rule 5 from rule 1, and a discriminating test needs the rule-1 screen that RV-15.19.4-1 (a) says is missing.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24 ("FUNCTION CONVERT. This function has been added to enable conversion between data representations"), read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.

subject: ORD function
notes: PB3 LANDED. ORD now returns the 15.70.4 r1 ordinal position for EVERY character, including one past the 256-entry weights table: the old c+1 fallback abandoned the collating sequence there and left ordinal 256 occupied by nothing. 12.3.7.4 GR7 1.3 places unspecified characters above the highest specified one in unchanged native order, which is the arithmetic NationalCollation.Weight already performed. Golden pins the derivation {A,B} at 1 / 0x00-0x40 at 2-66 / 0x43-0xFF at 67-255 / U+0100 at 256 / U+0101 at 257.

subject: ORD function
notes: Re-verified independently and it survives, including the edge that killed r1. Class national arrived with COBOL-2002, so r2 applies 2002+. The national table is SPARSE over the full 65,536 code units (AlphabetBindNationalLiteralPhrase: no & 0xFF mask, no fixed-size array) and NationalCollation.Weight computes an unspecified code unit's position as NextFree + (c − |specified codes below c|) — the §12.3.7 GR7 k3 arithmetic, which is correct under ALSO collapsing. PROBED: ALPHABET RN FOR NATIONAL IS N"A" ALSO N"B" with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL IS RN printed ORD(N"A")=00001, ORD(N"B")=00001, ORD(N"C")=00067 — all three match the hand-derived GR7 k3 values, and 00067 is exactly the case the alphanumeric r1 path gets wrong. Routing: BindIntrinsicCore sets CollateNat (never the alphanumeric Collate) whenever the argument's category is National, so the 256-entry alphanumeric table can never alias a national character; with no ALPHABET … FOR NATIONAL literal phrase in effect the identity body Ord(string) IS the r2 value (D-N3 code-unit order). Premise checks that killed two candidate findings: a NATIONAL GROUP item — the one shape whose category OperandCategory returns null for — is unreachable because GROUP-USAGE appears in no grammar rule and is explicitly not modelled; and a class-national-but-category-national-edited argument (PIC NBN), which would route to the alphanumeric weights, is loud-rejected at bind with COBOLNET0899 before ORD ever sees it. Both test-refs exist and pin ORD VALUES on the national path (char_national ORD=19991 on the native sequence; alphabet_national ORD-A=00003 and ORD-SP=00036 under a REV-NAT literal phrase).

subject: ORD-MAX function
notes: BindIntrinsicCore has no zero-length-literal guard for ORD-MAX, though the identical rule IS implemented for siblings (BindConvert tests `BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 }` for §15.19.3 SR1; CheckRepertoireArgs for §15.66.3 r3) — one rule written down in some places and not others. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV. subject: PI function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Pi() = Math.PI is a legitimate implementor-defined approximation of (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795), and the documentation obligation is discharged: Annex A.1 item 92 (validated - 'Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) ... The value returned does not have to be documented') exempts the VALUE while still requiring the characteristics/representation, and those ARE documented in CONFORMANCE.md SS7 (the row keyed '- (SS15.4.1 / SS14.9.11.4 GR1)', read and confirmed to state that a FLOAT-valued function renders through the same shortest-round-trip CobolFloat.Display a COMP-2 item does). PARTIAL for a receiver-shape leg, re-verified independently on the built CLI at --std 2023: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes through the ONE FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble's scaled double exceeds Int64 at scale >= 19 and SATURATES to long.MaxValue with no size error and no diagnostic - '01 R19 PIC 9V9(19). COMPUTE R19 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R19.' prints 0.9223372036854775807 and PIC 9V9(30) prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807. Neither is an approximation of pi, so rule 1 is violated for every legal 2002+ receiver of 20..31 digits (scale <= 18 is fine: PIC 9V9(18) prints 3.141592653589793280, within approximation license). ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.' at --std 2002 is rejected with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)'. SS15.73.3 rule 3 requires the returned value to be EXACTLY 3.141592653589793238462643383279503; PI is absent from the IntrinsicBinder staged-loud list (which holds only ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION) and rides the ordinary RenderFloat/Math.PI/binary64 path in EVERY arithmetic mode, so a STANDARD-DECIMAL program silently gets native binary64 digits. FAILING INPUT (re-run independently on the built CLI): 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PISDREV2. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9V9(17). PROCEDURE DIVISION. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R17.' at --std 2014 and --std 2023 prints 3.14159265358979328; rule 3 truncated to the receiver (COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates, SS14.7) requires 3.14159265358979323 - note the earlier draft's expected '...324' was the ROUNDED value and is wrong. At PIC 9V9(30) it prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 (the FromDouble Int64 saturation) against a required 3.141592653589793238462643383279. THE FALSE PREMISE, written in two places - the CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs class header and the IntrinsicBinder staging comment - is 'their returned-value rules are prose approximations, NOT equivalent arithmetic expressions, so the value is implementor-defined in EVERY mode (SS15.4.1 last paragraph)'. subject: PRESENT-VALUE function

The body `for (int i = 0; i < amounts.Length; i++) pv += amounts[i] / Math.Pow(1 + rate, i + 1)` is exactly Σ argument-2ᵢ / (1 + argument-1)^i for i = 1..n — §15.74.4 r1c, with r1a and r1b as its n = 1 and n = 2 cases — and §15.4.1 licenses 'an implementor-defined approximation' under native arithmetic. Verified with the built CLI: PRESENT-VALUE(0.100 1000 2000 3000) and the hand-written FUNCTION SUM EAE both give 4815.927873, which is also the exact hand-computed value. Annex A.1 item 92 ('Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) … The value returned does not have to be documented') means the documentation test does NOT downgrade the native leg, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md already carries a §15.4.1 / §14.9.11.4 GR1 row. THE PARTIAL: §15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect, and instead of doing so IntrinsicBinder rejects the program with DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic (COBOLNET0899, EditionSeverity.Error) — legal COBOL refused; confirmed by running an OPTIONS/ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE FIX SESSION: that staging condition is `ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.Standard or ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal` and OMITS ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, which §15.4.1 covers equally. subject: RANDOM function
notes: Neither half of 'it shall be zero or a positive integer' is enforced at bind or at run time, and the §15.3 raise ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') never fires for a RANDOM seed. (a) NEGATIVE: CobolIntrinsics.Float.Random(long seed) does `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))`, so a negative seed is silently ALIASED onto a large positive one — REPRODUCED: FUNCTION RANDOM(-5) and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483643) both return 636542013 (the alias is the two's-complement mask 0x7FFFFFFB, NOT abs(), so it does not even agree with .NET's own Random(int) sign handling). (b) NON-INTEGER: IntrinsicRenderer.IntArg truncates to scale 0, so FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75) silently becomes seed 1 — REPRODUCED: RANDOM(1.75) and RANDOM(1) both return 248668584. Concrete failing input: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(-5).` then `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75).` — compiles exit 0, zero diagnostics. The EC machinery EXISTS and is already used by sibling intrinsics (Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError — CobolDate's DATE-OF-INTEGER/DAY-OF-INTEGER range checks, CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble on NaN); RANDOM simply never reaches it, so `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` cannot catch it either. Fix shape: the seed range/integrality check belongs in the runtime body through ExceptionState.ArgumentError (a runtime-valued seed cannot be screened at bind), plus a bind-time diagnostic for the statically-known literal case. test-needed.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: BARE QUESTION: shall the §15.75.3 rule-4 implementor-defined seed be a FIXED value, so an un-seeded FUNCTION RANDOM sequence is reproducible across runs, or stay the current per-process entropy seed? Why this is not CONFORMS: the field initializer is `private static Random _random = new()`, and on .NET 6+ the PARAMETERLESS Random constructor seeds xoshiro256** directly from OS entropy — there is no seed VALUE at all, which is precisely what Annex A.1 item 144 ('RANDOM function (seed value when no argument on first reference). This item is required.') names as the required determination. Documentation is genuinely waived by item 144 ('The seed value used by the implementor does not have to be documented'), so this is NOT a CONFORMANCE.md gap — it is an unmade choice with an observed user-visible consequence: four consecutive runs of the same program gave first values 925010183 / 038930312 / 356550812 / 117861222. The in-code rationale also misdescribes the mechanism as 'the .NET time-derived default', evidence the behaviour was inherited from the framework rather than chosen, and no compiler survey is recorded (feedback_survey_compilers_on_latitude requires one before settling implementor latitude). subject: RANDOM function
notes: The runtime body conforms (Random.NextDouble() is in [0,1)) and the FLOAT-receiver path (num.Receiver.Real) hands the double through unquantized. The FIXED-POINT receiver path does NOT: RenderFloat wraps the call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in `(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`, so any returned value >= 0.9999999995 quantizes to exactly 1.000000000 — not 'less than one'. THE QUANTIZATION DEFECT IS DEMONSTRATED, not conjectured: on the same shared code path `01 R PIC 9V9(9). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999).` prints 1.000000000 while SQRT(0.999999998) prints 0.999999999. For RANDOM the top bucket is one draw in ~2.1e9 (the seeded back-compat generator's NextDouble is InternalSample() * (1.0/int.MaxValue) and only InternalSample() == 2147483646 clears the threshold; the argument-less xoshiro path has the same ~5e-10 probability), so no short deterministic COBOL input exhibits it — the bound is broken by the emitter's generic rounding, not by the generator. Fix shape: clamp (or round toward zero) at the quantization point for range-bounded functions instead of leaving the < 1 bound to FromDouble's AwayFromZero. test-ref conformance-test:...Random_SeededSequence_PinnedToSpec was STRUCK by review — its receivers are PIC V9(9), which has NO integer position, so a 1.000000000 result would silently store as .000000000, and the test asserts nothing about the range. nist:IF131A is kept as corroboration only (a NIST golden is a regression net, never spec-derived, so it cannot close the row); its WS-NUM is PIC S9(5)V9(6), which can represent 1.0, so its `WS-NUM < MAX-RANGE` legs would in principle catch the violation. test-needed: a spec-derived case pinning the < 1 bound on a receiver able to hold 1.0.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) constructs `new Random(int)`, which on .NET 6+ is pinned to the back-compatible (Knuth subtractive) seeded implementation — deterministic for a given seed. Re-verified across FOUR separate processes at four editions: FUNCTION RANDOM(5) returned 338369841 every time while the argument-less draws in the same programs varied, so the determinism belongs to the seeded path and is not process reuse. Independently corroborated WITHOUT using the compiler as its own oracle: a from-scratch reimplementation of the .NET seeded subtractive generator reproduces the compiler's output exactly for seeds 0 (726243270), 1 (248668584), 5 (338369841), 42 (668106466, 140907298, 125518289) and 2147483643 (636542013) — the sequence is algorithmically determined by the seed, not incidentally stable. subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) is computed exactly for fraction widths up to NINE digits — Analyze forms `((long)hh*3600 + mi*60 + ss) * 10^f + frac` at scale f, S correctly carrying the fractional-second digits of the seconds subfield (§15.3.3.2), and the offset/UTC subfields correctly NOT entering the sum; both D.31.5.9 worked examples reproduce exactly ("hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" → +18867.81). It breaks at TEN or more fractional-second digits: Analyze accumulates every subfield through a local `int val = 0;` and then does `case Fld.Fraction: frac = val;` even though `frac` is already a long, so the fraction wraps at 2^31 in unchecked arithmetic. Verified at --std 2014: `("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000")` into `01 WS-A PIC +9(5).9(10).` returns +45295.8705032704 instead of +45296.3000000000 (3000000000 − 2^32 = −1294967296); twelve digits `("hhmmss.ssssssssssss", "123456812479168304")` into PIC +9(5).9(12) returns +45296.000730349360 instead of +45296.812479168304; nineteen digits returns +00000.01. §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction width implementor-defined with a floor of nine; COBOL.NET neither enforces nor documents a maximum, and A.1 item 202 ('Time formats and corresponding function values (maximum precision not less than nine fractional digits)', required, 'This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7: NO — §7 currently lists only items 2, 59, 158 and 205–215. So the conforming fix is BOTH halves: widen the accumulator (or reject past the defined maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION) AND add the item-202 row to CONFORMANCE.md §7. The two existing tests exercise the expression only at 0 and 2 fraction digits, so nothing covers the overflow.

notes:

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED MECHANICALLY (python scripts/spec/cite.py --check):
  15.10.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK §15.10.2 (General format): <u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ASIN</u> ( argument-1 )
  8.4.3.1.2 "function-identifier-1" -> OK (Format 1 of an IDENTIFIER is a function-identifier)
