  14.9.2.3 "shall reference numeric data items" -> OK §14.9.2.3 2)
  14.9.13.2 "selection-object" -> OK §14.9.13.2 (General format)

THE FORMAT ITSELF IS CONFIRMED AND IS CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED. specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries the underlined transcription "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ASIN</u> ( argument-1 )" (the backtick form quoted in the input file is the stale copy in docs/rearchitecture/spec-rule-catalog.json). Two required words, exactly one argument, no bracketed or optional element. Verified against the compiler with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file> --run:
 - ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog's ASIN row is Fixed 1..1 and IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore's "args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs" arm fires. "COMPUTE X = FUNCTION ASIN" -> COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION ASIN takes 1 argument(s); 0 given"; "FUNCTION ASIN()" -> same; "FUNCTION ASIN(0.5 0.5)" -> "...2 given".
 - POSITIONS THAT WORK: COMPUTE, MOVE sending operand, DISPLAY operand, an IF relation on both sides, and PERFORM VARYING ... FROM — all yield 0.523598776 for ASIN(0.5).
 - ARGUMENT-1 SHAPES THAT WORK (§8.4.3.2.3 r8 admits identifier / literal / arithmetic expression): literal, signed literal, data-name, fixed subscript E(1), variable subscript E(I), arithmetic expression E(1) - E(2) (= ASIN(0.3) = 0.304692654), parenthesized (A), nested FUNCTION SIN(0.5) (= 0.500000000), and a COMP-2 item (the PB2 …Real route).
 - ASIN IS CORRECTLY NOT OVER-RESERVED (§8.11 lists it as an intrinsic-function-name, not a reserved word): "01 ASIN PIC 9 VALUE 3" coexists with FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) in the same program — ran it, printed X=0.523598776 and ASIN-ITEM=3.
 - IDENTICAL UNDER ALL FOUR EDITIONS: --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 each ran the COMPUTE/MOVE/IF program and produced the same values.

WHY THIS IS NOT CONFORMS — two positions where source written to this general format is legal COBOL and the compiler does not accept it. These are DEMONSTRATED failures, not merely unverified edges:

(1) THE FOUR ARITHMETIC STATEMENTS REJECT IT AT THE PARSER. A function-identifier is an identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 1); §8.4.3.2.4 r1 makes an intrinsic's temporary an elementary data item whose description is the function's (§15.10.1: "The type of this function is numeric"); §14.9.2.3 r2 asks only that identifier-1 "reference numeric data items"; and §8.4.3.2.3 bars a function-identifier only as a RECEIVING operand (r1) and only where an INTEGER operand is required (r11) — neither applies to ADD's sending operand. So this is legal COBOL, and I ran it:
    ADD FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) TO X
  -> error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'ADDFUNCTION'
     error COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near 'FUNCTION'
  Same raw-parse rejection, each re-run by me: "SUBTRACT FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) FROM X" ('SUBTRACTFUNCTION') and "DIVIDE FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) INTO X" ('no viable alternative at input FUNCTION'); unchanged under --std 85. ROOT CAUSE READ IN THE GRAMMAR (CobolParserCore.g4): addOperand, subtractOperand, multiplyOperand and divideOperand are each exactly "dataReference | literal" with NO functionCall alternative, while CobolExpressions.g4's primaryExpression does list functionCall. CROSS-CUTTING, NOT ASIN-SPECIFIC: I reproduced the identical rejection with "ADD FUNCTION LENGTH(S) TO X", so one grammar fix closes it for every catalogued function.

(2) EVALUATE TRUE WITH A RELATION CONDITION LED BY THE FUNCTION COMPILES AND THEN CRASHES AT RUN TIME. §14.9.13.2 lists condition-2 among the selection-objects. I ran:
    EVALUATE TRUE
      WHEN FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) > 0.5
        DISPLAY "BIG"
      WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "SMALL"
    END-EVALUATE
  -> Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: "EVALUATE TRUE/FALSE paired with a value WHEN object". CONTROLS I RAN THAT ISOLATE IT TO THE LEADING FUNCTION-IDENTIFIER: "WHEN X > 0.5" prints BIG; "WHEN (FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) > 0.5)" prints BIG; "WHEN 0.4 < FUNCTION ASIN(0.5)" prints GT4. Cause read in the source: evaluateWhenItem (CobolControlFlow.g4) orders "valueOperand" BEFORE "condition", ANTLR takes the first match, and EvaluateBinder.BindWhenItem then finds item.condition() null against a TRUE subject. Accepting-then-crashing is worse than a diagnostic.

WHY PARTIAL RATHER THAN DIVERGES: the ASIN format is implemented exactly as §15.10.2 draws it wherever the parser reaches it; the defect is that the format is not WIRED to every position the language permits a function-identifier. A future reader should treat this as a live gap, not a stylistic caveat — legal source is being rejected.

EDITIONS, ESTABLISHED WITHOUT READING IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn FIELD: a full-text search of specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns ASIN in exactly seven places — the table of contents, the index, §8.11 Intrinsic function names, the §15.6 summary table ("| ASIN | Num1 | Num | Arcsine of argument-1 |"), and §15.10 itself. It appears in NO Annex E added/changed list, so nothing in the 2023 standard marks it introduced or altered after 1985. CAVEAT RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: intrinsic functions entered the 85 line through the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment rather than base ISO 1989:1985, which is how this compiler models --std 85 (the CobolExpressions.g4 functionCall comment says exactly that); on that modelling all four editions apply, and I confirmed all four accept the format identically.

COVERAGE: no spec-derived test exists. A recursive grep of tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance and tests/conformance restricted to *.cs/*.cob/*.json returns only incidental substring hits (AsIntrinsicArguments, ReadViewAsInteger, "sending-OPERAND", SkeletonGate); there is no ASIN case anywhere. The only real ASIN references in the repo are the frozen legacy tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Runtime/IntrinsicFunctionTests.cs#Asin_ViaDispatch and the NIST goldens IF103A/IF401M — a legacy-oracle test and a NIST golden, neither of which may close a row.

ASIN is ABSENT from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (whose eleven rows are §15.7 and §15.70-15.79), so post-PB1 its argument class is still UNSCREENED. The extraction that produced this input dropped that clause; it should be re-extracted.

notes:
SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS: verdict SURVIVES as DIVERGES. I actively tried to soften this to PARTIAL (the natural overturn: "the FORMAT itself — required words, required parentheses, arity 1 — IS enforced; argument admissibility belongs to a §8.4.3.2.3 row") and the attempt FAILS on the grammar's own written contract, quoted below. CITATIONS, all re-validated mechanically this pass: §15.11.2 resolves; `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 8); `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 2); `cite.py --check 4.2.2 "syntactically distinguishable"` => OK. ⛔ The ONE-LEVEL-SHORT form FAILS and must not propagate: `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal"` => FAIL. Note the shipped COBOLNET1544 diagnostic text still carries the short form "ISO 8.4.3.2 SR7" — a real, separate citation-hygiene defect worth a sweep.

ENFORCED HALVES, each re-run by this reviewer at default --std 2023. Arity is closed in BindIntrinsicCore from IntrinsicCatalog.Build's Fixed 1..1 row even though `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` is a deliberate grammar superset: `FUNCTION ATAN` and `FUNCTION ATAN()` both give "error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION ATAN takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO 15.3)"; `FUNCTION ATAN(1 2)` gives "...2 given". OMITTED is correctly rejected: `FUNCTION ATAN(OMITTED)` gives "error COBOLNET1544: OMITTED shall not be specified as an intrinsic-function argument". `FUNCTION ATAN(1)` binds and returns 0.785398163.

DIVERGENCE — CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, actually run, exit 0 with ZERO compile-time diagnostics:

       01 R PIC S9(3)V9(9).
       ...
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(LEADING).

It fails only at RUN time: "Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... intrinsic argument 'LEADING'" (exit 127). `FUNCTION ATAN(TRAILING)` reproduces identically, so it is the whole phrase-word set, not one token.

PREMISE CHECKED, not just the rule (the CA12 trap). LEADING is a §8.9 RESERVED word — I grepped the §8.9 list and it is there, and I grepped the §8.10 context-sensitive list and it is NOT there — so it can never be a user-defined word and therefore never an identifier. §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 limits argument-1 to "an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression"; LEADING is none of the four. The violation is decidable from the token alone, and §4.2.2 requires it to be indicated.

WHY THIS BELONGS TO §15.11.2 AND NOT TO A §8.4.3.2.3 ROW — the point the softening attempt died on. The admission is structural: `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` with `fnArgPhraseWord : LEADING | TRAILING | LAST | FIRST | ANY | START | AFTER | ALPHANUMERIC | NATIONAL`. The grammar's own comment states the contract verbatim: "A superset rule: which words a given function admits is the binder's §15 job." The general format of §15.11.2 IS that §15 job for ATAN, and the binder has no arm discharging it — so the obligation the grammar delegates is the one this row owns. Those phrase words are legal only inside TRIM (§15.96), FIND-STRING (§15.37), SUBSTITUTE (§15.87) and CONVERT (§15.19). FIX SHAPE (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — the shape that makes the NEXT function automatic): the admissible phrase-word set belongs in the catalog row, empty for ATAN and for every function that takes none, screened once in BindIntrinsicCore with a drift test — never an ATAN-specific arm.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, correctly attributed AWAY from this row and re-verified. `COMPUTE R = ATAN(1).` with NO REPOSITORY paragraph also compiles clean and dies at run time with "NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'ATAN(1)'". Tempting to book under §8.4.3.2.3 SR2, but the premise does not hold: ATAN is a §8.11 intrinsic-function-name and is NOT in the §8.9 reserved-word list (grepped, no match), so without REPOSITORY it is simply an UNDEFINED data-name and the compiler is right not to bind it as the intrinsic. Control re-run: `COMPUTE R = ZQWXYZ(1).` fails identically — a general undefined-subscripted-reference hole (§8.4.1/§4.2.2) belonging to a reference-resolution row. The LEGAL keyword-omitted form was also re-run and is CORRECT: with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` the same `COMPUTE R = ATAN(1).` compiles and prints 00078539816C (+0.785398163).

EDITIONS: as for AR-15.11.3-1 — Annex E.2 item 13's list of names new in 2023 does not include ATAN, so 2014 and 2023 are established; §15.11.2 carries no edition qualification; the 85/2002 boundary is not establishable from this document, so all four per the brief's fallback, NOT from IntrinsicCatalog's MinEdition column.

test-needed. Verified on disk: nothing under tests/conformance/** mentions ATAN, and no unit or conformance-test method exercises the ATAN format, its arity or its argument admissibility. The covering test must be a NEGATIVE case asserting a compile-time reject of `FUNCTION ATAN(LEADING)`; conformance:negative/... is the right home.

subject: COMBINED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS. The general format carries TWO underlined REQUIRED words and only ONE of them is enforced. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.17.2 "COMBINED-DATETIME"` -> OK, format line `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>COMBINED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 )`. ENFORCED HALF (re-verified by me, not inherited): arity and the parentheses come from the catalog row (IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2) checked in BindIntrinsicCore - 1 argument, 3 arguments, `()` and a bare `FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME` with no parentheses each produce `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME takes 2 argument(s); N given (ISO 15.3)`; the space-separated form the format literally prints, `FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID WS-S12)`, binds as two arguments and returns the same value as the comma form; the edition gate emits COBOLNET1502 at --std 85 and --std 2002 and is clean at 2014/2023. UNENFORCED HALF - the required word FUNCTION. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required" -> OK): 'If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required.' CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run at --std 2023 AND --std 2014, with NO REPOSITORY paragraph anywhere in the program: `01 WS-ID PIC 9(7) VALUE 143951. 01 WS-SEC PIC 9(5) VALUE 45296. 01 WS-CD5 PIC Z(6)9.9(5). MOVE COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CD5.` -> compiles with ZERO diagnostics, exit code 0, assembly written; it fails only at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC)'`. The positive counterpart is correct (adding `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` makes the same statement print `REP= 143951.45296`), so `IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction` implements SR2's permission but nothing enforces its 'otherwise'. ATTRIBUTION, stated honestly: the mechanism is GENERIC unresolved-reference staging in `ExpressionBinder.RefFailure`, not an intrinsic-path defect - `MOVE ZZ-NOT-DEFINED(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CD5` behaves identically - so the fix belongs in name resolution; but the consequence is that this format's required word is not enforced, which is why the row cannot read CONFORMS. WHY THE PRIOR CONFORMS WAS NOT SAFE: its ALL-subscript evidence is false. It reported `WS-T(ALL)` 'rejected (expands to 3, arity error)', which was an artifact of a 3-element table. With a TWO-element table, `MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-T(ALL)) TO WS-CD5` compiles clean and prints `ALL= 143951.45296` - one argument specifier accepted where the format writes two. I do NOT downgrade on that, because §8.4.2.3.3 SR6 (cite.py-validated: 'The subscript ALL may be used only: - When the subscripted identifier is used as an intrinsic function argument') permits ALL in ANY intrinsic-function argument, which is broader than §15.3's 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times'; the two clauses are in tension and the compiler's acceptance is defensible under SR6. It is recorded because it shows the prior CONFORMS rested on an untested happy path. TEST: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob (read on disk, .out present) writes the general format at `MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CDT` and the golden pins `CDT= 153569.45296` - it covers the ACCEPT half only; test-needed for a negative fixture covering the arity rejections and the missing-FUNCTION rejection. EDITIONS: Annex E.2 item 13 establishes >= 2014 (COMBINED-DATETIME is not among the seven names new in 2023); the 2002/85 boundary is not derivable from this document, and the exclusion is asserted, not spec-derived. Not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED, both consequences re-run. THE ALTERNATIVES ARE RIGHT; THE POSITIONS ARE NOT. All four source words and all five destination shapes bind, with the 15.19.1 result type (NAT destination -> PicCategory.National, everything else Alphanumeric - re-verified: CONVERT(WS-N NAT NAT HEX) returns the digits as NATIONAL positions, 0030 0030 0034 0031). But BindConvert harvests EVERY keyword-shaped argument into `kws` irrespective of POSITION (`foreach (var a in argCtxs) { if (KeywordWordOf(a) is { } w && IsConvertFormatWord(w)) { kws.Add(w); continue; } operands.Add(...); }`), while the general format fixes `( argument-1 source-format destination-format )` (--check 15.19.2 "argument-1 source-format destination-format" -> OK).
(1) REJECTS LEGAL COBOL. ANUM/BYTE/HEX/NAT are CONTEXT-SENSITIVE words: I re-verified the 8.10 table rows in specs/ISO_COBOL.md - '| ANUM | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| BYTE | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| HEX | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| NAT | CONVERT intrinsic function |' - and 8.10's lead-in (--check 8.10 "treated as a user-defined word" -> OK) says a context-sensitive word used where it is NOT permitted in the general format is treated as a user-defined word. 8.9 reserves only ALPHANUMERIC, ANY and NATIONAL. Argument-1 is not a position where those four words are permitted, so a data item so named is legal there. Re-run:
       01 NAT     PIC XX VALUE "41".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(NAT HEX ANUM) TO WS-R.
-> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION CONVERT takes argument-1 source-format destination-format (ISO 15.19.2); 0 operand + 3 format keyword(s) given`. Expected SH=[A] (15.19.4 r1). The declaration itself is accepted, so only the CONVERT reference is turned away. Same defect for an item named ANUM, HEX or BYTE.
(2) ACCEPTS SYNTAX THE FORMAT DOES NOT ADMIT. Re-run: `CONVERT(ANUM WS-A ANUM HEX)` (source-format BEFORE argument-1) prints 41, and `CONVERT(ANUM ANUM HEX WS-A)` (argument-1 LAST, after the entire destination-format) also prints 41. The harvest is fully position-free.
Also latent: the IntrinsicCatalog row is `Add(new("CONVERT", IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 2, 4, "s", ...))` - min arity 2 where the format's minimum is 3 (argument-1 plus two format words), and the declared ArgKinds "s" is inert because CONVERT is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.
FIGURE CHECK - the transcription is FAITHFUL and the printed FIGURE is the defective artefact; do NOT 'fix' the compiler toward it. The destination-format figure uses braces throughout, which literally makes HEX mandatory in the non-BYTE branch. Three places in the standard's own PROSE contradict that and are decisive: the 15.19.1 type-table rows 'ALPHANUMERIC alone' and 'NATIONAL alone' (--check 15.19.1 "The type of this function depends upon the keywords in the destination format list" -> OK), 15.19.4 r1/r3 ('When the destination-format is ANUM / NAT'), and 15.19.4 NOTE 3 b. Rule 3 (source differs from destination) is also unstatable without bare ANUM/NAT destinations. The compiler treats HEX as optional and is RIGHT to.
Test-ref kept for the alternatives half only; it does not exercise the position rule - a position test is still needed.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.
